vignes.title: A heritage of old vines
vignes.intro: Their exact age is unknown. They may have been planted after the devastating frosts of 1956 that decimated the Bordeaux vineyards. But without knowing their precise planting date, their gnarled trunks speak for themselves…
vignes.p1: Old vines offer many advantages: naturally controlled yields, deep root systems that resist summer drought and draw minerals from lower soil layers, smaller grapes that are more concentrated and less susceptible to disease.
vignes.p2: These are massal selections — grown from plants that previous winemakers had empirically identified as producing the best juice. This means genuine genetic diversity, far removed from clonal selection where a single individual is replicated thousands of times, impoverishing the genetic heritage of the varietal.

terroirs.title: A mosaic of terroirs
terroirs.subtitle: 4 plots — 4 soils with distinct characters
terroirs.intro: The local geology has created a mosaic of soils that winemakers have long recognized. Plot boundaries were drawn accordingly.
terroirs.bardejats_text: The southern tip of the estate. On a gentle north-facing slope — ideal in a warming climate — the clay-limestone soil is typical of the Bordeaux region. The plot produces concentrated, rich grapes, perfect for a sweet wine.
terroirs.claux_text: Just below Bardejats, on a cooler clay-silt soil. It produces grapes with lower sugar levels, resulting in wines with less alcohol. The natural sparkling wine is made from this plot.
terroirs.artigues_text: Split between two zones: a clay-limestone area threaded with blue marl, and a sandy gravel zone common in the area. Both zones are blended to make the dry white wine.
terroirs.calcaire_text: All plots rest on a limestone layer beneath the plateau overlooking the Garonne and Ciron valleys. The rock lies just 30 to 50 cm below the surface. This friable limestone allows the vines to root deeply, drawing on coolness and moisture even in the height of summer. Even during heat waves, they avoid the water stress that halts growth, disrupts ripening, and weakens the plant. The limestone also imparts a freshness to the wines that balances perfectly with the natural roundness of the Sémillon grape.

philosophie.title: A respectful approach to the environment
philosophie.intro: The goal in managing the vineyard is first to create the conditions for a healthy plant.
philosophie.sol_text: No direct fertilisation of the vines, but amendments designed to stimulate soil life. Grass grows between the rows; only the area directly under the vine is weeded — by horse. In autumn, a cover crop of legumes is sown to fix nitrogen. Every three years, compost and manure are added to maintain soil fertility and its capacity to hold rainwater.
philosophie.maladies_text: Anti-mildew treatments comply with organic farming standards. Plant decoctions — particularly willow, horsetail and osier — are used to reduce copper dosages. Canopy management through spring bud removal also prevents the dense foliage that encourages disease.
philosophie.cheval_text: Using horses for under-vine weeding is a deliberate choice: less soil compaction, more precision, and a different connection to the vine. It also helps preserve the microbial life in the soil, which is essential to the vine's health.
philosophie.cheval_text2: Soil work is carried out with horses. It is precise work, respectful of the old, twisted vine stocks that sometimes have to be worked around. Here, the tool adapts to the vine, not the other way round. The estate is thereby helping to revive the trade of horse-drawn ploughman, whose benefits are being rediscovered today.
philosophie.bio_text: Since 2026, the estate has been pursuing organic farming certification. No green harvesting is practised — one of the advantages of old vines is that the plant naturally regulates its own crop load, without the vigour of its youth.

vins.title: The Wines
vins.subtitle: Classic wines… and beyond!
vins.intro: In the cellar, intervention is kept to a minimum. We simply let the grape's potential express itself.
vins.graves_sec_text: Aged in barrels for 10 months, given a silky texture through lees stirring, this is a delicate wine with floral and white fruit character. Enjoyable on its own, or paired with cheese and fish.
vins.graves_moelleux_text: Made from botrytis-affected grapes harvested in successive passes from late September to late October. A rare cuvée produced only in favourable years. Concentration and complexity are the hallmarks.
vins.rose_text: A gastronomic rosé, given a discreet ageing in old barrels — without oak influence, but with lovely roundness and rich aromatics. Perfect as an aperitif, and equally at home with spiced cuisine.
vins.petnat_text: To be drunk young. Grown on the cool soil of Les Claux, it has a low alcohol content and very fresh aromas. Serve well chilled.
vins.appassimento_text: A nod to our Italian friends! Made from fully ripe grapes air-dried for 2 to 3 weeks before pressing. The aromas stay fresh while the juice concentrates.
vins.mute_text: Aged for 3 years in barrels, this wine — rare in the Bordeaux region — shows how much Sémillon reveals its aromas when you know how to wait for it…

frederic.title: Frédéric Baysselance
frederic.subtitle: Winemaker in Landiras
frederic.p1: Château Baysselance was born in 2024 from a simple dream: to grow vines differently, in harmony with living things. Frédéric Baysselance acquired four plots in the commune of Landiras, at the western edge of the Graves appellation, where the last vineyard rows give way to the Landes pine forest.
frederic.p2: Captivated by the diversity of terroirs and convinced that vines must be tended with patience and humility, Frédéric chose from the outset to work with horses — a counter-intuitive decision, but one that reflects a deep philosophy: adapting to nature's pace rather than imposing his own.
frederic.p3: The old vines he took on are a precious inheritance. Their gnarled trunks carry the memory of the Bordeaux vineyard — a genetic diversity that modern clonal selection has often sacrificed in the pursuit of yield. Here, it is the plant that decides.
frederic.p4: Since 2026, the estate has been pursuing organic certification — a natural step for someone who never sought to farm any other way.
frederic.quote: "Vines need to be listened to. Once you learn to observe them, they tell you everything they need."
